ABOUT THE TEAM

OpenAI's mission is to ensure that artificial general intelligence benefits all of humanity. The Consumer Devices team is building a new generation of AI-powered products that seamlessly integrate hardware and software to create intuitive, transformative experiences. We bring together experts across embedded systems, machine learning, hardware, design, and product engineering to develop products at the intersection of AI and consumer technology.

ABOUT THE ROLE

OpenAI is seeking a System Performance Engineer to profile, benchmark, and optimize performance across our embedded hardware products. In this role, you will work across operating systems, applications, camera and vision, graphics, and platform teams to define product KPIs, build performance tooling, and drive optimizations from early lab characterization through product launch and real-world usage. You will help establish the performance standards that shape the user experience of our products, ensuring they remain responsive, efficient, and reliable throughout their lifecycle.

This role requires deep expertise in embedded or high-performance systems, strong operating systems fundamentals, and hands-on experience debugging under tight latency, power, and memory constraints.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of four days per week in the office and one day working remotely. Relocation assistance is available for new hires.

IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL:

- Develop system performance benchmarks, methodologies, and policies to evaluate end-to-end product behavior.

- Profile and analyze performance across key product use cases and workloads using custom and industry-standard profiling tools.

- Partner closely with engineering teams to identify bottlenecks and drive performance optimizations across the software stack.

- Define high-level product KPIs and establish measurement frameworks to measure launch readiness and monitor performance throughout the product lifecycle.

- Measure, report, and track metrics including system responsiveness, memory utilization, cold boot performance, long-term stability, and behavior under constrained conditions such as thermal limits and low battery states.

- Investigate field performance regressions and drive issues to resolution using data-driven analysis.

YOU MIGHT THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF YOU HAVE:

- Deep experience shipping embedded or high-performance systems on Linux, Android, or iOS devices.

- Strong proficiency in C/C++, Python, or Rust, with exceptional operating systems fundamentals, including process management, IPC, drivers, interrupts, power management, media frameworks, graphics, filesystems, and networking.

- A proven track record shipping real-time systems operating under tight latency, power, and memory constraints.

- Expertise with profiling and debugging tools such as Perfetto, GDB, LLDB, perf, ftrace, or Instruments.

- Experience building instrumentation, analytics, and performance tuning frameworks.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

- Familiarity with statistics, experimentation methodologies, or data science concepts.

- Experience collaborating cross-functionally with embedded software, systems, camera and vision, audio, graphics, applications, and hardware teams.

- Experience defining product KPIs, benchmarking methodologies, and launch readiness metrics for hardware products.

- Experience investigating field performance regressions and driving fixes through cross-functional collaboration.

jobs.description: Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world’s most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. Our Data Center Planning and Delivery (DCPD) organization builds and scales the infrastructure that powers AWS. We are seeking a Construction Estimator specializing in electrical scope to join the newly formed AMER Estimating and Cost Control (ECC) organization as a discipline subject matter expert. This is a technical individual contributor role. You will provide bottoms-up and top down electrical estimating capability for AWS data center construction across AMER and even globally in collaboration with EMEA and APJC Regional Estimating functions. Your focus spans the full electrical scope of a data center — medium- and low-voltage distribution, switchgear, generators and paralleling, UPS and battery systems, transformers, busway, feeders, grounding, lighting, fire alarm, and the electrical content of mechanical and controls packages. You will collaborate globally with estimating teams across all AWS regions on BOD cost inputs that inform design standards. When Design Engineering introduces a electrical design change or innovation, you are the first call — delivering rapid, discipline-specific cost impact assessments that enable informed decisions. This role is foundational to ECC’s mission of creating a structured feedback loop between estimate and actual, so estimates improve every cycle. Key job responsibilities - Produce detailed, bottoms-up electrical construction cost estimates — MV/LV distribution, switchgear, generators/paralleling, UPS and battery, transformers, busway, feeders, grounding, lighting, and fire alarm - Collaborate globally with regional estimating teams on Basis of Design (BOD) electrical cost inputs that inform design standards across all AWS regions - Deliver rapid cost impact assessments for electrical PDCM intercepts, first-of-kind designs, and innovation proposals from Design Engineering - Support new regions planning with electrical estimates for market entry — pre-GBT cost intelligence where local pricing data is thin - Perform detailed electrical quantity takeoff and pricing from one-lines, panel schedules, specifications, and design documents at all design stages - Develop and maintain the electrical cost database — unit rates, $/MW parametric models, and equipment pricing reflecting current market conditions and AWS standards - Serve as the electrical estimating SME for Estimating Managers, reviewing and validating 3P vendor electrical estimates - Analyze electrical subcontractor pricing, bid tabulations, and awarded contracts to identify trends, anomalies, and cost optimization opportunities - Benchmark electrical estimates against portfolio actuals through the estimate-to-actual feedback loop with Cost Control - Contribute to estimating tools and templates, incorporating lessons learned from completed projects into improved electrical estimating methodologies A day in the life Your morning begins with a quantity takeoff on a Design intercept from Design Engineering — a proposed switchgear lineup change that could shorten lead time but adds installed cost. You model the delta against the current BOD electrical estimate and prepare a cost impact memo for DE’s design review. Midday, you join a global call with electrical estimating counterparts in EMEA and APJC to align on BOD electrical cost inputs — medium-voltage distribution unit rates, generator $/MW, and UPS pricing — for the next design standard revision. Your AMER actuals are the benchmark. Afterward, an Estimating Manager asks you to gut-check a 3P vendor’s electrical estimate; you spot a conduit and feeder routing assumption that doesn’t match the latest one-line and flag it. You close the day updating your electrical cost database with final account data — a switchgear package landed 6% above estimate in a competitive-bid market. You document the driver and adjust unit rates for the next round of estimates. About the team AMER Estimating and Cost Control (ECC) is a newly formed organization within DCPD that unifies Estimating and Cost Control under a single leader. ECC provides end-to-end cost lifecycle ownership — from initial estimate through final account. You will be one of several Discipline Estimators (Electrical, Mechanical, CSA) working alongside the Estimating Managers who cover cluster groups across AMER, all reporting to the Manager, Construction Estimating (Chief Estimator Equivalent). Estimating provides the inputs — methodology, rates, benchmarks, discipline takeoffs, and 3P vendor products — that support Preconstruction’s owned estimates and CAR deliverables. Your electrical expertise directly supports both project-level estimating and global design standard development.

jobs.description: Purpose of the Role The Automation Senior Engineer is a member of the Site Digital & Automation Team and is responsible for the run‑state support, lifecycle maintenance, and continuous improvement of site automation and digital systems supporting manufacturing operations. This role provides hands‑on technical expertise to ensure production continuity, system reliability, validated state, and regulatory compliance. The role works in close collaboration with Operations, Engineering, and Core Digital & Automation partners. Responsibilities Automation Operations & Production Continuity · Provide day‑to‑day operational and technical support for production‑critical automation and digital systems. · Act as a key technical point of contact for Operations, Manufacturing, and Engineering partners for run‑state automation systems. · Support investigations, deviations, and unplanned events by providing automation subject matter expertise and technical root‑cause analysis. · Support NPI projects, new equipment introductions, and the transition of systems from project delivery into BAU operations. Automation Maintenance, Lifecycle Support · Maintain automation systems in a validated and compliant state, ensuring adherence to GMP, GAMP, and formal change‑management requirements. · Develop, update, and review automation lifecycle documentation including requirements, design specifications, SOPs, and periodic reviews. · Ensure statutory and regulatory maintenance requirements are met and support regulatory audits and inspections as required. Incident, Crisis & Business Continuity Support · Participate in real‑time incident response for automation and digital systems, including fault diagnosis, escalation, and recovery support. · Collaborate with site, network, and core Digital & Automation support teams to restore system availability and minimise production impact. · Support site Business Continuity Plans (BCP) execution and testing · Operate in alignment with site SLAs and response targets · Document incidents, root causes, and resolution actions · Engage and coordinate with vendors as required Control Systems & Automation Infrastructure Management · Provide hands‑on technical support across the automation lifecycle for DCS, PLC, SCADA, HMI, and PC‑based production systems. · Design, test, deliver and manage automation software across its lifecycle, from initial introduction through to retirement, in line with site coding standards and good engineering practices. · Implement system and software changes using formal change‑control and validation processes. · Support the specification, supplier engagement, development, installation, and commissioning of automation system upgrades. Process Automation & Continuous Improvement · Contribute to automation and manufacturing systems continuous improvement initiatives using Lean / Six Sigma methodologies. · Apply strong analytical and problem‑solving skills to improve system reliability, data integrity, and operational performance. · Participate as a technical contributor in cross‑functional problem‑solving and standardisation initiatives. · Contribute to continuous improvement initiatives within assigned systems or areas Key Attributes, Skills & Competencies · Strong understanding of business processes and operational acumen within manufacturing environments · Expert knowledge of manufacturing automation systems including DeltaV DCS, PLCs, SCADA, and PC‑based platforms. · Strong understanding of automation lifecycle management and experience in supporting audits in regulated / validated GMP environments. · Proven troubleshooting and root‑cause analysis skills in operational manufacturing environments. · Ability to work independently while collaborating effectively with cross‑functional teams.
